ui.explodeNote: Disciplines lift apart in height order: lighting drops below the walls, then ductwork, cable tray and pipework rise in turn. Spreading pushes every part outwards from the corridor’s centreline.

blocks.p: An AutoCAD 2018 drawing (format AC1032, 3.2 MB) exported from a Revit 3D view named “3D - nkucita”. It holds 3D mesh geometry only. There is no text or dimensioning, and both paper space layouts are empty.
Everything is trimmed to a Revit section box 11.38 m long, 3.18 m wide and 1.60 m deep. Units are millimetres, and every coordinate in this viewer is a model coordinate.
The host file is the MEP model. It carries all 451 service parts. Walls and a second copy of the lighting arrive through linked models.

blocks.small: Revisions are read from the link names. The two interiors links carry “4” and “03” in their names, which may be revision numbers.

blocks.p: The check found 17 major and 13 minor clashes, plus 8 places where surfaces only touch. Zone 3 holds 32 of them, between X -2,046 and -1,278.

In zone 3, Geberit HDPE drainage bends and branches sit up to 66 mm into the top of ducts [[D-10]] and [[D-08]]. Two Ø114 pipes, [[P-063]] and [[P-064]], run straight through duct D-10 together with their insulation. Their fittings suggest welded stainless steel. A Ø200 drainage pipe and its fittings cut through cable tray bends [[TF-27]], [[TF-30]] and [[TF-31]].
Away from zone 3, Ø22 copper pipe [[P-100]] passes fully through the inclined duct [[D-18]]. Drainage pipe [[P-057]] crosses the upper duct’s insulation zone.

9 downlights and 3 PIR detectors exist twice. One set belongs to the MEP model. The other sits inside the architectural link. Plan positions match to within 5 mm, and in every pair the MEP copy is 275 mm higher.

Either the two models assume different ceiling levels, or the architectural link carries an old copy of the lighting. Both sets also clip the side of the lower duct’s insulation by about 19 mm at DL-07 and DL-08.

Services meet the linked walls at 69 points. 38 pass through a modelled builder’s work hole. 22 have no hole, and now carry 16 proposed openings sized to the service. 9 run along a wall face rather than through it.
Every opening, with its services, clearance and fire-stopping, is in [[tab:open|Openings]]. Violet markers are crossings with a proposed opening.

Fused connection unit [[FCU-05]] sits 11 mm into the casing of fire damper [[FD-03]], and [[FCU-04]] sits 9 mm into cable tray [[T-30]]. Victaulic elbow [[PF-84]] reaches about 12 mm into the upper duct’s insulation.
Three links (external, bedrooms and amenities) contribute nothing inside this section box. Two of the three fire escape signs in the architectural link also have no geometry here.
Four 6 mm plates sit on the duct sides ([[DP-01]] to DP-04). They could be access panels or the stubs of branch connections. The file records no purpose for them.

blocks.small: Pipe systems come from Geberit HDPE drainage, copper press-fit, Victaulic grooved fire protection and welded stainless fittings. Each pipe takes the system of the fittings it connects to.

blocks.p: The DWG was converted to DXF with LibreDWG 0.13.3 and read with ezdxf. LibreDWG only partly supports the MATERIAL objects in this format, so material assignments were lost. Every layer in the file is set to colour 7, so the colours here are assigned by discipline.

Revit exported ducts, tray and walls as loose flat plates. Plates on the same layer that share vertices were joined into single solids. A second shell around a duct or pipe on the same centreline was treated as insulation. Duct insulation measures about 90 mm and pipe insulation about 50 mm.

Clashes were found by triangle-level mesh intersection (FCL through trimesh) between disciplines, and between each service and the walls. A part fully enclosed inside another without crossing a surface would be missed.

Grades work as follows. Major means two physical parts overlap by at least 25 mm, or by half the smaller part’s size. Minor covers smaller overlaps and any overlap involving inferred insulation. Touch means the surfaces meet with no measurable overlap. Overlap figures come from intersecting bounding boxes, so they overstate the overlap at bends and inclined runs.

holeSchedule.intro: X, Y and Z are model coordinates in mm from NCW_COORDINATED_CORRIDOR.dwg. Check them against the setting-out grid before marking out.

notes.label: Ref
notes.text: One reference per opening, numbered along the corridor from low X to high X. The same reference tags the opening in the model viewer.

notes.label: Location
notes.text: X and Y set out the centre of the opening on plan. Z centre and Z underside give its height. All values are model coordinates in mm.

notes.label: Status
notes.text: Modelled openings are hole families in the MEP model. Proposed openings mark services that cross a wall with no hole modelled, sized to the service.

notes.label: Clearance
notes.text: Gap from the service, or its insulation, to the opening edge. Needed: 25 mm all round for pipes, 50 mm for ducts and cable tray.

notes.label: Fire-stopping
notes.text: Proposed from the service type. Wall fire ratings are not recorded in the model. Confirm against the fire strategy before installation.

notes.label: Site check
notes.text: Initial and date once the opening is marked out and checked against this schedule.
